short: Ensemble-to-student distillation (M02, M06, M13) is standard: same-modality distillation predates it; 85.9% is one unseeded split of unstated unit, and 7x smaller is against six models.
position: KDE-SSI [@lai2023kdessi] changes three components: ensemble soft targets (M02), a single distilled decoder (M06), and reported time and size (M13). All three are standard: same-modality distillation of word classifiers was published for lip reading three years earlier [@ma2021towards]; only the ensemble teacher is new, on one split. "7.0× smaller, 20.8× faster" compares the student with six models (N = 6, Table II) on a GPU (Fig. 5): N explains the size ratio, not the speed ratio. The comparison that matters, student against one ResNet1D (85.9% vs 81.2%, Table II), is one split with no seed or repeats reported and an unstated grouping unit (§IV.E), and the student's architecture is not given. So 85.9% is not comparable with the later subject-independent 85.8% on the same words [@hong2026cvos], and deployment (§V.B) is unmeasured.
